brief: Citadel Securities' Frank Flight argues market internals have been pricing a growth slowdown for months while the 10Y yield and consensus earnings estimates have not caught up. His X-MIG factor, built from ten cross-asset internal ratios, has fallen from +2 standard deviations in mid-year to -1.85 now, with nine of ten inputs contributing negatively over the past three months. Against that, the 10Y yield sits at +1.75 standard deviations, leaving a 3.5-sigma gap Flight calls historically large, driven by inflation and a hawkish Fed rather than growth. Flight expects the damage to surface first as a flatter curve, then a broader growth reassessment. The resilience obscuring this, he argues, rests on AI capex, whose contribution to GDP growth is set to roughly flatten in 2027 even as dollar spending keeps rising, while political backlash against data centers (per colleague Nohshad Shah) and frontier-lab margin pressure threaten the buildout underpinning both his growth and rate-hike calls. In 2018 and 2022, similar gaps resolved with stocks catching down to internals, not the reverse.
